name: taking seats from the end of an empty row leaves no orphan
leaving one seat at the end of an empty row is an orphan
leaving a single gap beside a sold seat is an orphan
taking the middle of a row can strand a seat at both ends
an unavoidable orphan is allowed when the free run has exactly one seat more than needed
the same unavoidable case holds whichever end is left
a seat that was already isolated is never the buyer's fault
filling a free run completely leaves no orphan
splitting a party across a row can strand the seat between them
a pair left between the party and a sold seat is fine
a single seat segment cannot be orphaned by taking it
taking one seat from a run of two is unavoidable
taking one seat from the middle of three strands both neighbours
